title: Chapter 7
content:
After a two-hour drive, the car pulled up to a location a short distance outside Seoul.

Stepping out of the sedan, Jakyeong stared at the structure before him, momentarily speechless. Calling it a "house" was a severe understatement—it was a sprawling estate. Endless stone perimeter walls stretched in every direction, blanketed by a lush, thick carpet of climbing red roses that matched the exact hue of the bouquet in his hands.

Two security guards stationed at the heavy main gates approached and bowed respectfully. As they passed through the entryways, the true scale of the compound became clear; the interior grounds were far more massive than they appeared from the outside.

Jakyeong’s very first thought was, I'm screwed.

His second thought was, Where the hell did he hide the safe?

Crossing the manicured courtyard, they entered the main house, where two more armed guards stood at attention. That made four so far. While there might be more scattered around, four wasn't an absurdly high number given the sheer size of the estate. In fact, the domestic staff seemed to outnumber the security detail.

As Jakyeong offered a polite nod to the passing maids, an elderly, silver-haired man approached from the far end of the foyer.

"Welcome, young master. You must be exhausted after such a long journey."

The old man greeted him warmly. Judging by his immaculately tailored attire, he was likely part of the senior household staff. Given his advanced age, he had probably served this house for decades. Knowing it never hurt to build rapport with key staff, Jakyeong bowed respectfully and flashed a shy, gentle smile.

Beside him, Kang Il-hyun slipped off his suit jacket, tossing it onto a valet stand before loosening his tie with a quick tug.

"Tae-soo will show you to your quarters. Go unpack, then come back downstairs."

Jakyeong gave a docile nod.

Tae-soo grabbed the heavy luggage and led the way toward a narrow side corridor at the edge of the living room. Following close behind, Jakyeong took the opportunity to scan the interior. Thanks to sweeping floor-to-ceiling glass windows, the estate felt surprisingly bright and warm. Given that Il-hyun had survived multiple assassination attempts, Jakyeong had expected a gloomy, heavily fortified bunker. This airy aesthetic was an unexpected twist.

Then his eyes caught a subtle dome on the ceiling: a high-definition security camera.

Looking closer, he spotted identical units stationed everywhere—by the front gate, near the entrance, and sweeping the main living hall. As he cataloged their locations and blind spots, he accidentally bumped right into Tae-soo’s back.

The man had stopped in front of a sleek set of metallic doors and pressed a call button.

"Ah, I'm so sorry," Jakyeong stammered, putting on a flustered act. "I was daydreaming..."

"No harm done," Tae-soo replied neutrally.

The elevator doors glided open, and the two stepped inside.

Scanning the control panel, Jakyeong’s eyes narrowed slightly. The buttons weren't limited to standard first and second floor indicators. Directly beneath the 1st-floor button sat a unique interface—not a numbered panel, but a glowing biometric fingerprint scanner.

A restricted level.

Jakyeong took mental notes, but before he could inspect it further, the doors chimed open on the second floor. Tae-soo stepped out first, with Jakyeong trailing right behind.

"There's... an elevator in the house?" Jakyeong asked, tilting his head with innocent wonder.

Tae-soo gave a single nod, carrying the luggage down the hallway. "Yes. However, you are free to use the central staircase for daily transit."

"I noticed a button underneath the first floor. What's down there? Is there a basement?"

Tae-soo came to a sudden halt, turning around to stare down at Jakyeong.

Holding the rose bouquet against his chest, Jakyeong widened his eyes, beaming a look of pure, childlike curiosity. He did his best to project the aura of a harmless, inquisitive rich kid.

Tae-soo, however, offered no answer. He simply turned back around, his long strides cutting through the quiet corridor.

They passed several closed doors along the long hallway, every single one fitted with an electronic smart-lock. Jakyeong quietly counted the rooms in his head until Tae-soo finally stopped in front of the very last door.

Tae-soo tapped an encrypted keycard against the panel, and the heavy door unlocked with a quiet chime.

Stepping inside, Jakyeong nearly broke character. This wasn't just a guest bedroom—it was a fully self-contained luxury apartment built inside the mansion, complete with its own private lounge, kitchenette, and master bedroom suite.

Jakyeong looked around, still clutching his bouquet. "It's... wonderful."

"I am glad it meets your approval," Tae-soo said smoothly. "Housekeeping will arrive daily at 11:00 AM to service the suite. If you require any specific amenities, you may notify me or the staff directly. Meals can be prepared and sent up at your convenience."

"Thank you, I—"

Jakyeong froze mid-sentence.

Mounted high in the corner of the private lounge was another security camera. Cold anxiety prickled his skin. He stepped deeper into the suite to check the master bedroom—sure enough, a second lens stared right down at the king-sized bed.

Jakyeong tossed the roses onto the mattress, his brows furrowing in genuine irritation. What the hell is this?

Driven by paranoid instinct, he pushed open the master bathroom door to check. Fortunately, there were no visible lenses inside... though that didn't rule out pinhole cameras hidden in the fixtures.

Mildly infuriated by the total lack of privacy, he stepped back out into the lounge. "Excuse me, Mr. Park... about the room—"

The words died in his throat.

Tae-soo was gone. In his place, Kang Il-hyun sat casually on the leather sofa, crossing his legs.

Jakyeong bit his lower lip slightly, running through his mental checklist: Do not snap. Do not glare. Keep it sweet. Frail young master. Pampered rich kid. Timid and easily startled.

Stepping forward into the lounge, he forced a troubled, uneasy expression onto his face. "There are... security cameras... in the bedroom."

"They're installed in every room," Il-hyun replied smoothly, adjusting his cuffs. "Does it make you uncomfortable?"

"Well... yes," Jakyeong murmured, lowering his gaze. "It feels... a bit like I'm being watched..."

"Consider it a layer of protection," Il-hyun said, his tone utterly devoid of warmth. "A precaution, if you will."

"A... precaution?"

"If you happen to get murdered on my property, Yi-an, it would create quite a headache for me," Il-hyun said coldly. "I'll need clear video footage for the investigation."

"..."

"That was a joke. You're not laughing."

"A-Ahaha..." Jakyeong forced a nervous, strained chuckle.

"Don't force it," Il-hyun said mildly. "If it bothers you that much, I'll have the staff dismantle the camera in the bedroom."

"Yes... please. I'd appreciate that."

"And if an emergency ever arises..." Il-hyun gestured toward a sleek black intercom mounted on the lounge wall. "...see that panel? Pressing button '1' connects you directly to the staff quarters downstairs. They'll come up immediately. Button '0' dials directly into my private suite, though I doubt you'll ever have reason to use it."

"Right..."

"If a life-threatening situation occurs, retreat into the bathroom immediately. There's a panic button installed inside as well."

Jakyeong blinked. "A... life-threatening situation?"

"Hmm." Il-hyun paused, as if pondering the possibilities. "Say, high-caliber rounds coming through the exterior glass. Or an assassin rappelling down from the roof to breach the windows. Or perhaps someone standing over your bed at 3:00 AM, swinging an axe toward your skull."

"Haha..."

"Why are you laughing? I'm being entirely serious."

"..."

"We lost two guards here a few years back," Il-hyun continued casually. "I had all the glass upgraded to military-grade ballistic plating afterward, but we haven't had an intruder since, so I haven't been able to test its durability yet. Let's hope we don't have to test it while you're staying here."

Wang Han’s warnings flashed through Jakyeong’s mind: There have been multiple assassination attempts on Kang Il-hyun. Every single hitman sent after him died violently.

It wasn't an exaggeration. The rumor was 100% true.

"I... I see..." Jakyeong managed to utter.

"That covers the basics," Il-hyun said, standing up from the sofa. "Do you have any questions for me?"

Where is your hidden safe? Is it in the basement? I need to get inside, so would you mind lending me your thumb? If you don't want to walk down there with me, feel free to chop it off and hand it over. I can slice it off real nice for you if you'd prefer.

If he asked that out loud, Il-hyun would probably slit his throat on the spot.

Jakyeong forced a sweet, innocent smile and shook his head side to side.

Il-hyun’s eyes lingered on his face once more, probing him with that intense, unreadable stare. Jakyeong held the smile so hard his cheek muscles began to cramp. No one slaps a smiling face, right? God, just get out of my room. Why is this so uncomfortable? Leave already. Get out.

As if receiving the unspoken telepathic plea, Il-hyun smoothed his trousers and turned toward the door.

"I have an evening engagement to attend to, so I'll be taking my leave. Make yourself at home."

"Thank you... Director Kang."

"My younger brother will be arriving tomorrow," Il-hyun added, stopping at the threshold. "He's the same age as you, so you'll probably find him easier to talk to than me. If there's anywhere in the city you'd like to visit, just tell him. He has a bit of an edge to his personality, but once you get on his good side, he can be quite useful."

A younger brother?

According to his dossier, Il-hyun had two half-siblings. Whichever one was coming tomorrow, Jakyeong was certain they’d be ten times easier to deal with than this walking ice sculpture.

Nodding politely, Jakyeong squeezed out another innocent smile. Now beat it, he chanted silently in his head.

Just as Il-hyun reached the door, he suddenly halted and spun around.

"Ah. One more thing."

"Yes...?"

"Did you say you were an art major?"

Il-hyun’s face remained passive, but his dark pupils narrowed slightly, locking onto Jakyeong's face.

Jakyeong kept his breathing steady, answering with practiced ease. "Fine arts."

"Fine arts," Il-hyun repeated softly.

"Sculpture, specifically."

A look of realization flickered across Il-hyun’s face, and he gave a slow nod. "Ah. That explains it."

He didn't elaborate on what "it" was.

Jakyeong’s stomach dropped. He knew precisely what Il-hyun meant. Ever since that handshake at the airport, the man had been suspicious. Why would a frail, coddled young master raised in extreme wealth have dense, hard calluses on his hands? Especially in the exact spots unique to individuals who handled heavy firearms and combat blades daily?

By claiming to be a sculpture major, the heavy calluses from chiseling stone and handling metal tools suddenly made perfect logical sense.

"Enjoy your evening."

The moment the heavy door clicked shut and Il-hyun was gone, Jakyeong let out a long, ragged breath he had been holding in his chest. He collapsed heavily onto the leather sofa.

Grabbing a decorative throw pillow, he raised his arm to hurl it violently at the door—then remembered the ceiling camera staring down at him and checked his swing mid-air.

Instead, he buried his face deep into the velvet cushion and let out a muffled, silent scream.

Playing the role of a delicate, timid rich kid was driving him utterly insane. To make matters worse, the lack of a real cigarette was triggering severe nicotine withdrawal, fraying his nerves to a sharp edge.

After fuming into the pillow for a few minutes, Jakyeong dragged himself into the bedroom to unpack.
